validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all confirmed independently of GEM. The row is a real, FERC-jurisdictional delivery lateral: Vector Pipeline, L.P. filed an Oct 15, 2019 prior-notice request under its blanket certificate (Docket CP98-135) for a 1.24-mile, 24-inch lateral in St. Clair County, MI, connecting to DTE Electric's new 1,100 MW Blue Water Energy Center (Federal Register 2019-23841, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/11/01/2019-23841/notice-of-request-under-blanket-authorization-vector-pipeline-lp, mirrored at govinfo.gov). The U.S. EIA's own 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical workbook (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Oct2022.xlsx, tab 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)') carries a line item named exactly 'Blue Water Energy Center (BWEC) Pipeline', operator 'Vector Pipeline', Docket CP20-4 (the follow-on formal certificate proceeding), Completed 2021-12-15, Miles=1.25, Diameter=24, Additional Capacity=180 MMcf/d, Cost=$21.5M, State=MI/MI/MI (no state border crossed) -- an exact or near-exact match on every physical spec against the GEM row. This EIA line is almost certainly the true source underlying the sheet's own (unusable) [4] citation to the EIA naturalgas/data.php homepage -- that URL is a generic data portal and fails url_verifier's name check (does not mention 'Blue Water' or 'Vector' anywhere), so the sheet's own citation for this segment was effectively broken even though the underlying fact (this EIA workbook entry) is real and independently verifiable once you go find the actual document. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType='transmission' is the best fit of GEM's three allowed values (transmission / gathering / distribution) for a FERC Natural-Gas-Act-jurisdictional, large-diameter (24-in) delivery lateral off Vector's interstate transmission mainline (42-in, 1,745 MMcf/d) to a single industrial/power customer -- it is not a gathering line (no wellhead collection) and not a distribution main (not an LDC network); the Mountaineer Gas Company rows elsewhere in this batch are the correct contrast case for actual distribution. DUPLICATE CHECK against the roster: P3202 'Vector Gas Pipeline / Blue Water Compressor' (len 0, cap 380, recorded end state Wisconsin) is NOT the same project as P2505 and is not a duplicate/relabel. It is a completely different underlying entity that GEM's own wiki page conflates by name only: P3202 is the 'Bluewater Compression Project' (FERC Docket CP19-471) built by BLUEWATER GAS STORAGE, LLC -- an unrelated gas-storage company with a compressor station in Macomb County, Michigan restoring 500,000 Mcf/d of firm delivery capacity at its own interconnect with Vector, serving Wisconsin LDC customers (Wisconsin Gas, Wisconsin Public Service, Wisconsin Electric) who hold storage capacity there -- see cross_row_leads. 'Blue Water Energy Center' (DTE's power plant, St. Clair County) and 'Bluewater Gas Storage' (a storage operator, Macomb County) are two different 'Blue(w)ater' entities roughly 30 miles apart, not one pipeline recorded twice; P3202's Wisconsin endpoint is real and explained, not an attribution error. Opened 6 of the row's 7 harvested wiki citations (bit.ly resolved to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vector_Pipeline and read; Enbridge factsheet, offshore-technology.com, and the EIA homepage all read but are about the Vector MAIN LINE only and do not name BWEC; freep.com 2015 and ogj.com 2014 are pre-2019 Vector system news about a since-shelved unrelated expansion/bidirectional-flow proposal, read via their citation context since freep.com itself blocked live fetch -- neither is about this lateral). gascompressionmagazine.com (403, Cloudflare-style block, not a confirmed 404 -- not retired) is about the P3202 compressor project, not this row.

Two independent federal sources agree with each other and disagree with the sheet: (1) the Federal Register notice of Vector's Oct 2019 prior-notice filing states 'The total cost of this Project is approximately $21.5 million' (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/11/01/2019-23841/notice-of-request-under-blanket-authorization-vector-pipeline-lp); (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently records Cost (millions)=21.5 for the same named line item (Docket CP20-4). Neither figure is $22,000,000. The $0.5M / ~2.3% gap is not huge, but it is a real, reproducible number in two independent primary documents, so I'm not staging a REFS_ADDED ref against the current $22M value -- that would pair a verified citation with a figure the citation itself contradicts. Recommend pasting $21,500,000 instead.

validity.recommendation: re-verify Delayed/DelayType; no source found supports an actual delay -- consider blanking Delayed rather than leaving 'yes'/'inferred' unsupported
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet carries Delayed='yes', DelayType='inferred' for this row, but every timeline anchor I found describes an ordinary, on-schedule FERC project cycle with no reported holdup: prior notice filed Oct 15, 2019 (Federal Register 2019-23841) -> formal certificate docket CP20-4 (per EIA, implying filing in early 2020) -> construction completed and in service Dec 15, 2021 (EIA workbook) -- about 2 years from filing to service, unremarkable for an NGA Section 7/blanket-certificate lateral of this size, including through the 2020 COVID-affected construction season. I found no FERC notice of schedule change, no trade-press report of a slip, and no operator statement describing a delay. Per the controlled-vocab notes, 'inferred' means a GEM-rule dormancy/date-mismatch inference rather than a sourced claim, and ProposalYear/ProposalMonth were BLANK on the sheet before this pass (I've now filled ProposalYear=2019 as a fill[] object) -- it's plausible the 'inferred' delay flag is a stale artifact of that blank ProposalYear rather than a real finding. I can't positively prove a negative, so I'm flagging this as a validity concern rather than silently deleting the flag; contested value is left blank because I have no evidence for what (if anything) the correct value should be, only that 'yes' is unsupported by anything I could find.

validity.recommendation: keep Capacity=180 MMcf/d as-is; note one conflicting weaker source for the record
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=180 MMcf/d is corroborated by two independent primary sources: Vector Pipeline's own 2018 customer meeting presentation slide lists 'DTEE Interconnect ... DTE Electric - Bluewater Energy Center (DTEE-BWEC) ... near St. Clair, Michigan ... 180 MDth/d load' (vector-pipeline.com), and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently records Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)=180 for the same named project. Both also agree the lateral is DESIGNED to expand to 525 MMcf/d / 525,000 Dth/d with future compression/equipment upgrades (stated in both the Federal Register notice and the wiki's own EIA-derived prose) -- that 525 figure is a different, forward-looking design-max number and is not itself in conflict with the sheet's 180. CAVEAT: one industry trade source, nsenergybusiness.com's Blue Water Energy Centre project profile, states the power plant 'will receive up to 80 million dekatherm (Mdth) of feed gas a day from the Vector gas pipeline' -- a materially different, lower figure. Given it conflicts with two more specific, dated primary documents (the operator's own engineering slide and EIA's project-tracking dataset), I'm treating 180 as the correct, better-supported value and not contesting it, but flagging the conflicting number here per the read-everything-to-exhaustion rule rather than silently dropping it.

cross_row_leads.facts: P3202 ('Vector Gas Pipeline / Blue Water Compressor', recorded Michigan->Wisconsin, len=0, cap=380) is the 'Bluewater Compression Project', FERC Docket CP19-471, filed by BLUEWATER GAS STORAGE, LLC (not DTE, not the Blue Water Energy Center power plant) -- a new compressor station in Macomb County, Michigan (single 11,150-hp gas turbine/centrifugal compressor unit) at Bluewater's existing 20-inch interconnect with Vector Pipeline, restoring the originally authorized 500,000 Mcf/d firm delivery capacity (from a pressure-limited ~120,000 Mcf/d). Bluewater has long-term service agreements with Wisconsin Gas LLC, Wisconsin Public Service Corp, and Wisconsin Electric Co, who by 2021 held >95% of Bluewater's storage capacity -- this is exactly why the row's EndState/Province is Wisconsin: the customers, not the physical compressor, are in Wisconsin. Explains the roster's odd Michigan->Wisconsin endpoint; not an error. EIA's workbook independently carries this as a separate line item ('Bluewater Compressor Project', operator 'Bluewater Gas Storage', Completed 2021-11-19, Cost $40M, Capacity 380 MMcf/d, Docket CP19-471) -- matches the roster's cap=380 and completion timing exactly, and confirms it is unrelated to Blue Water Energy Center.
